descriptions: A force-directed photo archive that uses colour similarity to surface unexpected visual neighbours, then tests those relationships against human review.
photo-graph-browser.main_text: Dexter Young / projects / photo-graph / Index Dark Photography / Data visualization Photo Node-Gallery A force-directed photo archive that uses colour similarity to surface unexpected visual neighbours, then tests those relationships against human review. Launch experience Stack Next.js · D3 · Supabase Model selection Browsing photographs by colour. Photo archives are usually organised by time, place, or subject. This experiment asks whether colour can offer another route through the work: moving from one photograph to another through light, tone, and palette. An initial CIE76 graph was visually dense yet still split natural neighbours apart. I tested five models against seven reviewed query sets; Mean LAB with CIEDE2000 gave the strongest result using the existing image features, so it drives the live graph. Reviewed set 100 photographs / 7 queries Selected model Mean LAB / CIEDE2000 Reviewed top four 89% relevant / 263 edges / 0 isolates Select a query photograph Human-reviewed affinity set Q 01 / ID 14 Snow / pale neutral Q 02 / ID 46 Dense neutral texture Q 03 / ID 49 Magenta performance light Q 04 / ID 57 Dark monochrome Q 05 / ID 65 Warm amber interior Q 06 / ID 69 Woodland green Q 07 / ID 112 Deep blue atmosphere Active query / ID 14 Snow / pale neutral “Relevant” marks a reviewed match. P@4 is the share of the first four results judged relevant; pair agreement measures how closely a model follows the reviewed ranking. Unmarked results are unjudged, not automatically wrong. Model 01 Mean LAB / CIE76 Query / 14 1 . ID 20 2.18 2 . ID 12 2.79 3 . ID 11 3.08 4 . ID 45 4.24 5 . ID 94 4.83 Relevant 6 . ID 16 5.43 Relevant in top four 86% Ranking agreement 82% Graph 246 edges / 7 component s Build time 3.7 ms Model 02 Mean LAB / CIEDE2000 Best reviewed P@4 Query / 14 1 . ID 20 2.14 2 . ID 12 2.74 3 . ID 45 3.40 4 . ID 11 3.70 5 . ID 94 5.16 Relevant 6 . ID 16 5.25 Relevant in top four 89% Ranking agreement 82% Graph 263 edges / 1 component Build time 9.5 ms Model 03 Mean Oklab Query / 14 1 . ID 20 0.010 2 . ID 45 0.015 3 . ID 11 0.019 4 . ID 103 0.028 5 . ID 39 0.029 6 . ID 94 0.032 Relevant Relevant in top four 75% Ranking agreement 66% Graph 260 edges / 2 component s Build time 2.5 ms Model 04 Oklab Distribution / Hellinger Query / 14 1 . ID 11 0.039 2 . ID 94 0.067 Relevant 3 . ID 20 0.086 4 . ID 15 0.089 Relevant 5 . ID 29 0.095 6 . ID 45 0.108 Relevant in top four 82% Ranking agreement 76% Graph 291 edges / 1 component Build time 3.6 ms Model 05 Oklab Palette / Earth Mover Query / 14 1 . ID 94 0.065 Relevant 2 . ID 15 0.069 Relevant 3 . ID 11 0.072 4 . ID 103 0.073 5 . ID 29 0.075 6 . ID 20 0.079 Relevant in top four 71% Ranking agreement 65% Graph 274 edges / 2 component s Build time 152 ms Broad dominant-colour and tonal affinity, judged from the generated contact sheet. These are editorial judgments, not semantic labels or exhaustive relevance sets. Exact all-pairs benchmark / 4,950 pairs / generated 26 Aug 2026 Project readout A different way through the archive. The graph does not try to identify what a photograph depicts. Instead, it turns 100 photographs into a field of visual neighbours, then tests that field against 7 deliberately different reference images before anyone is asked to browse it. 01 / Index Photograph set The archive remains image-first. A feature pass records colour signals for every photograph, while the original image stays at the centre of the experience. 02 / Review Similarity test Seven query images define the kind of visual relationship worth preserving. Five colour models are checked against those judgments instead of assuming numerical closeness matches the eye. 03 / Browse Living graph The selected model becomes a force-directed gallery. It makes colour clusters and surprising near-neighbours available to browse as a field, rather than a fixed list of results.

It makes colour clusters and surprising near-neighbours available to browse as a field, rather than a fixed list of results.
